utakata 0.2.0 brings Shinobido 2 to Android, adds French and Spanish, a mouse camera, Xbox button prompts, cheats, skipping the intro logos and rePatch mods. The release now carries its compiler, so the first build downloads only the PS Vita firmware and asks nothing of Microsoft; it can also build without internet, from files you downloaded before.

## Downloads

| System | Download | Start |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, x64 | `utakata-v0.2.0-windows.zip` | `shinobido2.exe` |
| Linux x64, Steam Deck | `utakata-v0.2.0-linux.tar.gz` | `shinobido2.x86_64` |
| macOS 13.3+ on Apple Silicon | `utakata-v0.2.0-macos.tar.gz` | `Shinobido 2 - Revenge of Zen.app` |
| Android 9+, 64-bit ARM with Vulkan | `utakata-v0.2.0-android.apk` | **Shinobido 2** (install the APK) |

On a PC, unpack the archive and start the game. The first time, its importer asks for your own dump of Shinobido 2: Revenge of Zen (US PCSE00015, with update 1.02; the Mirror Spirits add-on is optional), downloads the PS Vita firmware from Sony (about 180 MB; the compiler is in the download), and builds the game on your computer in a few minutes. From then on the program goes straight to the game. Nothing of the game is in these downloads. See the [installation guide](https://github.com/vita-recomps/utakata/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md).

On Android (made for Snapdragon handhelds such as the AYN Thor), install the APK and start it: its setup screen builds the game on the device from your dump, in about 8 minutes on a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2. A PC that has built the game can also put it on the device (`--android`).

macOS: the app isn't signed by a registered Apple developer, so macOS refuses it the first time. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click "Open Anyway".

## New

* **Android** (64-bit ARM with Vulkan): the game built on the device from your dump, Turnip offered on Adreno, on-screen controls for phones with a **CROUCH** button that holds R, and **Import a Vita save** on the icon's long-press menu.
* **Language:** the game's English, French or Spanish text, and the system dialogs with it (**Language** on the settings menu's Game page).
* **Mouse camera** on a PC: Tab or a middle click captures the cursor, and the mouse turns the camera, up to the game's own speed. Sensitivity and inverted vertical on the Mouse page. The cursor hides by itself when the mouse is still, or when you play with a key or a gamepad.
* **Xbox button prompts:** A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, Menu and View in the game's prompts, its HUD and the Basic Controls page, or whichever the connected gamepad has (**Button prompts**).
* **Cheats** on the settings menu's Cheats page, all off: infinite health, infinite ninja tools and items, one-hit kills, maximum money and maximum stats.
* **Skip intro logos** (off by default).
* **rePatch mods**, kept beside the game and read in place of its own files. Add-ons and mods can be added after the build, in seconds.
* **The compiler comes with the release; no Microsoft licence.** The game's code is compiled with zig on Windows too, as on Linux and macOS: the first build downloads only the PS Vita firmware (Windows downloaded about 650 MB before), and there is nothing to accept. The downloads are about 90 MB larger.
* **Building without internet.** `--download-only <folder>` saves what the setup downloads; a build then takes the files from that folder (`--offline <folder>`, the importer's "Downloaded files" row, or a folder named `offline` in the game's folder). Firmware files you already have work too, whatever their names. See [Without internet](https://github.com/vita-recomps/utakata/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#without-internet).
* **Fallback downloads.** When Sony's server doesn't answer, the setup takes the same files from the Wayback Machine's copies, checked by SHA-256.
* **RecompLauncher:** each release carries a `recomplauncher.json`; when the launcher runs the setup again with the same release and dump, it ends at once ("Already built").
* From ss-delta's front end: an Exit page in the settings menu, and laptops with two GPUs use the faster one.

## Fixed

* **Linux and the Steam Deck: the update in the same folder as the game could be left out**, and the setup stopped with "eboot.bin is not a build this port supports". The game is now always installed first, and the setup says when the update is missing.
* **Games copied straight off a Vita** carry the PSN account's own licence, usable only on that Vita: the setup now says so before its downloads and takes the NoNpDrm licence in the dump's `license/` folder instead.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0

Unpack 0.2.0 over your game's folder (replace the files), then start the game with `--install` and build again from the same dump: this release's front end needs the game's code built by it. Saves and settings are kept. See [Updating](https://github.com/vita-recomps/utakata/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#updating).

Every release's changes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/vita-recomps/utakata/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

SHA-256 and build attestations: see the files attached, and `gh attestation verify`.
